messages.content: The Boston quality-systems conference is confirmed for September 15 through 17. The Monday workshop starts at 8:30 a.m., and the program ends Wednesday at 4:00 p.m. I need Sunday travel from San Francisco. Compare returning Wednesday evening with staying until Thursday morning, and include the conference hotels before the block closes.

I’ll build both schedules around arrival Sunday, September 14. Before I total them, is the conference at the Boston Convention and Exhibition Center, and should I include the $1,690 registration and workshop fee in the authorization amount?
Yes to both. I need to be present for the entire workshop and closing session, so do not show a Wednesday flight that requires leaving early.

The practical outbound choices are a United nonstop leaving SFO at 8:30 a.m. and reaching BOS at 5:08 p.m., or a Delta nonstop from 10:20 a.m. to 7:05 p.m. The United itinerary leaves more time for a normal hotel check-in and Sunday dinner. Paired with a Wednesday 6:45 p.m. return, United is $486 round trip; paired with Thursday’s 7:15 a.m. return, it is also $486. Delta is $512 with a Wednesday 7:25 p.m. return or $528 with a Thursday 8:10 a.m. return.
Is 6:45 Wednesday genuinely workable after a 4:00 finish? I do not want a plan that works only if everything runs exactly on time.

It is possible but tight. From the convention center, you would need to retrieve your bag immediately and leave around 4:15. A taxi or rideshare to Logan commonly takes 15 to 30 minutes then, but traffic or a delayed closing session could reduce the airport margin. The Silver Line is more predictable on cost, though the transfer and walking make it slower with luggage. I would treat the 6:45 flight as feasible, not comfortable.
Then show the hotels and the full cost difference. The lowest conference rate looked farther away, but I could not tell whether the savings survived transportation.

Three conference-block options remain. The Westin Boston Seaport is about a five-minute covered or mostly covered walk from the convention center and totals $951 for Sunday through Wednesday or $1,268 through Thursday. The Omni Boston at the Seaport is roughly a seven-minute walk and totals $1,098 for three nights or $1,464 for four. The Aloft Boston Seaport is the least expensive at $884 for three nights or $1,176 for four, but it is about a 15-minute walk and less convenient with a conference bag or poor weather. All totals include room tax.
Compare the Westin and Aloft more carefully. Include airport transportation in both directions, and assume I will take a car to Logan if I fly Wednesday.

For the Wednesday-return version, I would allow $35 for a rideshare or taxi from either hotel to Logan after the conference. On Sunday, the free inbound Silver Line from Logan serves the Seaport; from the World Trade Center stop, the Westin is the easier walk. Reaching Aloft generally adds another short walk or a local transit connection. Allowing $5 for incidental transit, ground transportation is about $40 for Westin and about $45 for Aloft. The Aloft therefore saves about $62 overall: $884 plus $45 versus $951 plus $40.
And for Thursday morning? I assume the early flight changes the airport plan.

Yes. For a 7:15 a.m. departure, plan to leave the hotel around 5:15 a.m. by taxi or rideshare. I would budget $35 for that trip. Sunday can still use the free Silver Line, with a small transit allowance if needed. Estimated local transportation is $40 from the Westin and $45 from Aloft. The four-night lodging difference remains $92, so Aloft saves about $87 after the transportation allowance.
Give me complete totals for four combinations: Westin Wednesday, Aloft Wednesday, Westin Thursday, and Aloft Thursday. Use the $486 United fare and registration.

Using registration at $1,690, airfare at $486, and the ground estimates: Westin with Wednesday return is $3,168 ($1,690 + $486 + $951 + $40). Aloft with Wednesday return is $3,105 ($1,690 + $486 + $884 + $45). Westin with Thursday return is $3,484 ($1,690 + $486 + $1,268 + $40). Aloft with Thursday return is $3,397 ($1,690 + $486 + $1,176 + $45). Meals and any airline bag fee are not included.

The Wednesday options are cheaper, but I am concerned about carrying luggage into the last day and then watching the clock. Can the Westin hold the bag after checkout, and how late would I reach San Francisco on each return?

The Westin confirms complimentary luggage storage for registered guests after checkout. The Wednesday nonstop leaves BOS at 6:45 p.m. and arrives SFO at 10:25 p.m. local time. The Thursday nonstop leaves at 7:15 a.m. and arrives at 10:55 a.m. Thursday. The Thursday plan adds one hotel night but removes the need to leave promptly after the closing session.
Check whether the Thursday United fare includes a standard seat and carry-on. Also, is the 8:30 Sunday flight nonstop?

The quoted $486 itinerary is regular economy, not basic economy. It includes a standard seat assignment and one full-size carry-on plus a personal item; a checked bag would cost extra. Both segments are nonstop: SFO to BOS Sunday from 8:30 a.m. to 5:08 p.m., and BOS to SFO Thursday from 7:15 a.m. to 10:55 a.m.

Use Thursday and the Westin. The covered walk and not having to manage a rushed airport departure after the conference are worth the difference. Reconcile the authorization figure, but separate the core bookings from estimated local transportation.

The core booking subtotal is $3,444: $1,690 conference and workshop registration, $486 round-trip United airfare, and $1,268 for four nights at the Westin Boston Seaport. Estimated local transportation is $40, making the authorization request $3,484 before meals and any checked-bag charge. Compared with Westin and a Wednesday return, the Thursday plan costs $316 more, entirely from the additional hotel night; the airfare and transportation estimate are unchanged.
Is the Westin block still cancellable, and when does the rate expire? I need enough detail to send this for approval today.

The conference rate is currently available for September 14 through 18. It requires a card guarantee, with cancellation permitted without penalty until 6:00 p.m. Boston time on September 11; after that, one night plus tax is charged. The lodging block is scheduled to close Friday at 5:00 p.m. Boston time, but rooms can sell out earlier. The United fare is currently ticketable at $486 and may change until purchased.
Summarize the authorization-ready itinerary and identify what is reserved versus only quoted.

Authorization-ready plan: fly United nonstop from SFO Sunday, September 14 at 8:30 a.m., arriving BOS at 5:08 p.m. Take the free Silver Line to the Seaport and check in at the Westin Boston Seaport for four nights. Attend the 8:30 a.m. workshop Monday and the full conference through 4:00 p.m. Wednesday. Check out Thursday, September 18, leave by taxi or rideshare around 5:15 a.m., and fly United nonstop from BOS at 7:15 a.m., arriving SFO at 10:55 a.m.

The conference and workshop registration is confirmed at $1,690. The United itinerary is quoted at $486 but not ticketed. The Westin room is available at a quoted $1,268 including tax but is not yet reserved. Core bookings total $3,444; adding $40 estimated local transportation produces a $3,484 authorization request. Meals and a checked bag, if used, remain outside that figure.
